subject: Rosetta: proposed availability uplift and guaranteed response SLA
messages:
From: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@rosetta.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: availability uplift for pilot

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we discussed, Rosetta is entering a pilot where latency spikes during peak inference windows have real production impact. To approve budget internally we need a short written commitment around availability and a target P99 tail latency for the pilot period.

Specifically: can Redwood commit to a 99.99% availability target for the dedicated pool serving Rosetta with 15-minute incident response and an upgrade path to 99.995% if the pilot hits the usage thresholds? We understand that may require custom routing or capacity reservations — we are willing to discuss an uplifted commitment fee.

Attaching a one-page expectation doc; happy to sign a short appendix.

Best,
Carl
Account Lead, Rosetta AI

Attachment: pilot-availability-expectations.pdf

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@rosetta.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: availability uplift for pilot

Carl — thanks for the clarity and the PDF. Looping in Vivek (infra/routing), Rachel (SRE), and Marcus (legal/pricing) to confirm feasibility and implications.

High level asks from our side while we scope this:
- Are you expecting a full 24/7 SLA or business-hours support for the pilot?
- What traffic profile do you expect (QPS, avg tokens per request, peak window length)?
- Would Rosetta accept a staged commitment (99.99% during pilot, evaluate and ramp to 99.995% on successful thresholds)?

We can put together a draft appendix for signature once we confirm technical feasibility and cost.

—Neha

Attachment: rosetta-sla-uplift-proposal-v1.pdf

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: availability uplift for pilot

On Tue, Jul 12, 2027 at 10:05 AM Neha wrote:
> Carl — thanks for the clarity and the PDF. Looping in Vivek (infra/routing), Rachel (SRE), and Marcus (legal/pricing) to confirm feasibility and implications.

Quick operational readout:
- Achieving 99.99% for a dedicated pool is doable if Rosetta agrees to reserved capacity (m4-dedicated with a 20% buffer) and uses the regional failover we proposed.
- 15-minute incident response (pager) requires a PSR on-call escalation — we can offer it as a paid add-on during the pilot window; otherwise our standard SLO for alerting is 30 minutes.
- P99 tail latency target depends heavily on request size and batching. For small chat-like prompts (<=32 tokens) we can hit P99 <220ms on nvL6 instances; longer sequences will change that.

I will draft a rough runbook for the failover and a capacity profile. Rachel — can you weigh in on compliance and runbook acceptance criteria?

—Vivek

From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: availability uplift for pilot

Neha / Vivek —

Notes from SRE perspective:
- We need a runbook review and a postmortem SLA clause to be agreeable to both parties. For 99.99% uptime we will require:
  - Pre-warm and capacity reservation plan (Vivek to provide numbers).
  - Defined maintenance windows (max monthly downtime budgeted vs. exception handling).
  - Acceptance tests for failover (we will schedule a blue/green failover exercise before start).
- Also flagging that claiming a 99.995% target is a much tighter budget (approx 2.6 hours vs 8.8 hours of allowed annual downtime). That will constrain maintenance and require extra redundancy across AZs and possibly regions.

Marcus — please confirm what contract language we should use about credits and remedies. If legal needs a hardened appendix, share a template.

—Rachel

Attachment: rosetta-runbook-draft.docx

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 16:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: availability uplift for pilot

All — I reviewed the operational notes and the draft proposal. From a contracting perspective:
- We can offer a tiered appendix: Pilot: 99.99% availability with a capped credit of 25% of the monthly pilot fee per month for failures; Post-pilot upgrade to 99.995% requires a 3-month stability run and explicit capacity payment.
- The 15-minute incident response will be listed as 'targeted response' with defined on-call windows and an opt-in 'urgent pager' addendum.
- Wanted to call out indemnity/limitation language — we should avoid hard unlimited uptime guarantees; use 'commercially reasonable efforts' and measurable remedies only.

Neha — if you approve this approach I will circulate an appendix template and mark it for an expedited sign-off path.

—Marcus
